applicable_when: The kernel loads in_ptr0 with address formula `x0 + 3136*r0_2 + 301056*x1`. With XBLOCK=128, each warp covers 32 consecutive x0 (spatial) values — that dimension is coalesced. However, the reduction loop iterates r0_2 over 96 channels with a stride of 3136 floats (12 KB) between consecutive channel values. This means each iteration of the reduction loop issues a load that jumps 12 KB in memory, causing L1 misses on every access (4.3% L1 hit rate) and only 1/32 bytes utilized per cache sector (MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule). Additionally, XBLOCK=128 with R0_BLOCK=512 allocates large Welford accumulator arrays in shared memory per block, limiting occupancy to only 3 blocks/SM (18.75% theoretical). The grid of 245 blocks across 132 SMs yields only 0.62 waves, leaving most SMs idle. Reducing XBLOCK (fewer spatial positions per CTA) and setting R0_BLOCK=96 (cover all channels in one pass, eliminating the loop) reduces shared memory per block, increases blocks/SM, and improves the ratio of work per memory transaction. Autotuning explores the Pareto frontier of these parameters.
